label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires almost only on the last step of length-3 sequences (t=5, input is the fed-back second original token, model outputs the third original token; prev2_tok is <DEL>). L=3 holds 94% of activation mass, t=5 holds 92%. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on a token at its first occurrence. Magnitude depends somewhat on the input token: the strongest activations have inputs j, v, 3, p, i, and some inputs such as w often leave it below threshold (most of the ~8% false positives). Missed activations are weak: the copy step at t=4 in L=3, which is the first fed-back token, and scattered small firings near the end of longer sequences, e.g. L=4 at t=6 and L=9 at t=17.

issues: Upheld; every claim reproduces on the test split: precision 0.920, recall 0.709, F1 0.8007, mass recall 0.915.
The F1 barely clears the 0.8 bar. Recall is low because weak activations are missed: the predicate covers only 21% of the lowest-quartile activations, but 98-100% of the top two quartiles.

The claims I checked hold: zero activations in the original and delimiter phases (phase<2 gives precision 0), zero on first occurrences (in_first==1 gives precision 0), L==3 holds 94% of the activation mass and t==5 holds 92%, and adding in_count==1 lowers F1 (0.78).

Missed activations: L==3 & t==4 has precision 0.11 and only 2.5% of the mass, L==4 & t==6 has 2.3%, and L==9 & t==17 has 0.7%. These are minor, not a systematic class worth adding. Widening to (L==3)&(t>=4) drops F1 to 0.62.
False positives (209 on test) are spread over many inputs (w, m, n, r, l, ...). Excluding w gives test F1 0.798 and excluding 5 tokens gives 0.737, so there is no single token-based exception.
Gating on correct==1 changes nothing: identical scores.
The label 'final copy step of length-3 sequences' matches the predicate exactly and does not overclaim.

Data caveat: the store is features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store. Its dev split has 99,999 sequences (about 200k in total). Nothing in the tool output shows it was built from the 1/5 subsample in features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, so whether this baseline used the user's new data is still unverified.
